title: Ops incident communication blueprint
content:
Purpose
This blueprint is a compact, pragmatic draft for incident communications at Redwood Inference. It focuses on clear, timely customer-facing updates (status page + customer emails), tight internal war-room coordination, and a lightweight approval/sign-off flow so we avoid delays on critical announcements.

When to use this document
- Platform-impacting incidents (service degraded, partial outage, complete outage)
- Any incident where latency or correctness SLOs are violated for > 5 minutes
- Customer-visible data plane degradations or control-plane auth/credential outages

High-level goals
- Fastest possible detection -> acknowledgement -> first public notice (< 15 minutes target for high-severity)
- Consistent tone and cadence across channels (status.redwood.ai, customer emails, account reps)
- Minimize confusion: put mitigations and next steps up front, technical details later
- Keep internal stakeholders informed with concise actions and owners

Roles & responsibilities (communication-specific)
- Comm Lead (primary): owns external messages, coordinates approvals, posts status page. Typically the on-call SRE with comm training or the SRE lead if comms-sensitivity is high.
- SRE Lead: owns technical triage and provides status updates to the Comm Lead.
- On-call Engineer: executes mitigation playbook and provides timestamps for key actions.
- CS/Account Rep Liaison: drafts targeted customer emails for affected accounts and surfaces customer concerns back to the war-room.
- Engineering Manager (Escalation): decision authority for major rollbacks, cross-team mobilization.
- Legal & Security (when needed): review messages involving PII, data loss, or compliance language.

Severity classification & communication cadence
- Sev 1 (Full outage/critical SLO break): First public post within 10–15 minutes. Updates every 15–30 minutes until recovery.
- Sev 2 (Partial outage/major degradation): First public post within 30 minutes. Updates every 30–60 minutes.
- Sev 3 (Minor, intermittent): Post if issue persists > 4 hours or affects a significant feature set. Updates every 4–8 hours.

Channels & audience matrix
- Public status page (status.redwood.ai): All incidents with customer impact. Single source of truth for public-facing timeline.
- Targeted customer email: For customers showing errors or high error rates (> 1% of requests or high-value accounts).
- Internal war-room Slack channel: For operational coordination and time-stamped logs.
- Exec/ops summary email/Slack: For Sev1 and customer-impacting Sev2.
- Support ticket annotation (Zendesk/Jira): Add incident ID and link for any affected support threads.

War-room checklist (first 30 minutes)
1) Triage & acknowledge
   - On-call posts acknowledgement in primary war-room channel with incident ID and high-level symptom.
   - SRE Lead sets severity and documents initial detection time.
2) Appoint Comm Lead
   - If no trained comm lead present, SRE Lead nominates the on-call SRE as temporary Comm Lead.
3) Snapshot & evidence collection
   - Collect top-3 failing metrics (error rate, p95 latency, request volume) with timestamps.
   - Capture relevant traces and recent deploys (git sha, rollout time).
4) Customer impact determination
   - CS liaison queries: which accounts show errors? Are any enterprise customers affected?
   - If yes -> prepare targeted email list and coordinate with account owners.
5) Messaging & distribution plan
   - Draft a short status page entry (see templates below).
   - Decide whether to send a customer email and which accounts.
6) Stabilize & mitigation
   - Define immediate mitigation actions (traffic reroute, scale up, revert deploy). Assign owners.
7) Timing & cadence
   - Set next update time (15/30/60 minutes depending on severity). Add calendar reminder or pinned Slack message.

Status page templates (short, use placeholders exactly as shown)
- Initial notice (Sev1/Sev2)
  Title: Degraded service affecting text generation API
  Body: We are investigating elevated error rates and increased latency for the text generation API. Impact: some customers may experience 5xx errors or slow responses. Time detected: {{DETECT_TIME}} UTC. Status: Investigating. Next update: {{NEXT_UPDATE}} UTC. Incident ID: {{INCIDENT_ID}}.

- Update (progress)
  Title: Investigating — mitigation in progress
  Body: We have identified increased error rates on cluster us-east-1 and are routing traffic around the affected nodes. Impact: partial degradation for requests routed to the affected capacity. Mitigation in progress: traffic reroute started at {{MITIGATION_START}} UTC. Root cause analysis is ongoing. Next update: {{NEXT_UPDATE}} UTC.

- Resolution
  Title: Resolved — text generation API restored
  Body: The text generation API has recovered and error rates are within normal bounds. Service has been restored as of {{RESOLVE_TIME}} UTC. We will publish a post-incident report with timeline and root cause analysis within 3 business days. If you continue to see issues, please contact support@redwood.ai and reference Incident ID {{INCIDENT_ID}}.

Customer email templates (concise, avoid jargon)
- Initial targeted notification
  Subject: Incident notice — temporary disruption to text generation (Incident {{INCIDENT_ID}})
  Body: Hi {{CUSTOMER_NAME}},

  We’re investigating a disruption that may affect text generation requests for some customers. You may see increased latency or 5xx errors starting at {{DETECT_TIME}} UTC. Our team is actively working to mitigate the issue. We’ll send another update by {{NEXT_UPDATE}} UTC.

  We apologize for the disruption and appreciate your patience.

  — Redwood Inference Operational Team

- Customer follow-up (post-mitigation)
  Subject: Update — incident {{INCIDENT_ID}} — service restored
  Body: Hi {{CUSTOMER_NAME}},

  The incident impacting text generation has been resolved as of {{RESOLVE_TIME}} UTC. We have mitigations in place and are monitoring for recurrence. We will share a short incident summary and any relevant recommendations within 3 business days. If you noticed errors in your integration or need assistance, reply to this email or open a support ticket and reference Incident {{INCIDENT_ID}}.

  — Redwood Customer Success

Tone & guidance for public messages
- Keep language simple and customer-centered: focus on impact and next steps.
- Avoid speculative root causes in early updates. Phrase technical hypotheses as "we are investigating whether..."
- Use active voice and present tense for clarity.
- If unavoidable downtime for specific customers occurred, include a targeted apology and offer support.

Internal escalation & approvals
- For messages that mention customer data exposure, legal must sign off before posting. Aim for < 30 minutes turnaround for review.
- For Sev1 stating a broad outage or SLA miss, notify Execs (email+Slack) immediately after the first public post.
- CS/Account owners should be looped in before targeted customer emails go out (concurrent drafts OK).

Post-incident actions & communications timeline
- Within 24 hours: initial post-incident summary shared with SRE, CS, and product owners.
- Within 72 hours: draft RCA shared internally (root cause, timeline, action items).
- Within 3 business days: public incident report published on Confluence and linked from the status page if appropriate.

Record-keeping & tagging
- Tag every message with Incident ID and a link to the war-room channel.
- Update the incident artifact (Jira or internal tracker) with full message history and timestamps.

Sample simulated timeline (example)
- 09:03 UTC — Monitoring alert: p95 latency > 3s for text-gen.
- 09:04 UTC — On-call acknowledges in #war-room-tg, Incident ID INC-20260212-001 created.
- 09:06 UTC — SRE Lead sets severity to Sev1; appoints Comm Lead.
- 09:12 UTC — Initial status page post published (first notice).
- 09:20 UTC — Traffic re-route begins; CS notifies three affected enterprise accounts via targeted email draft.
- 09:45 UTC — Error rate back to baseline; remediation confirmed.
- 09:50 UTC — Resolution update posted to status page; customer follow-up emails sent.

Maintenance & training notes
- Runbook owner: eng-sre (Priya Shah) — review quarterly or after every Sev1 incident.
- Conduct one tabletop exercise per quarter focused on communications (rotate product area).
- Keep a language bank of pre-approved sentences for legal/security scenarios to accelerate approvals.

Open questions & TODOs for this draft
- Define measurable SLA for "first public post" (this draft suggests < 15m for Sev1; need exec alignment).
- Automate initial status page creation from monitoring alerts to cut human latency (prototype JIRA linked above).
- Create per-account impact extraction script to auto-generate targeted email recipients.

Appendix: quick copy snippets
- Short apology sentence: "We sincerely apologize for the impact and are prioritizing restoration of full service."
- Escalation ask: "Please join the war-room at <link> if you can help validate mitigations."
- Sign-off stamp: "Approved by Comm Lead: {{COMM_LEAD}} at {{APPROVAL_TIME}} UTC"

End of draft.
